purpose: Define how navigation charts, coordinate datums, transformation knowledge, instruments, and ship capabilities evolve across human history while remaining compatible with one authoritative spatiotemporal universe.

coreDistinction.authoritativeWorldState: Canonical object identities, physical state, motion models, and simulation time in declared world frames.
coreDistinction.navigationChart: A versioned representation of selected world state, expressed relative to a named origin, axes, epoch, model, and available observations.
coreDistinction.shipNavigationSolution: A vessel's estimate of its own state and destination state using its instruments, onboard computation, charts, clocks, communications, and calibration.
coreDistinction.rule: Changing a chart's origin changes the coordinates and mental model used to describe a journey; it does not move the stars, shorten the route, or improve a ship's sensors by itself.

frameHierarchy.principle: Frames are composable and time-aware, not a single forever-fixed hierarchy. Each transform declares source frame, target frame, epoch/time, units, orientation convention, origin state, model version, uncertainty, and validity.

transformRules: Never transform coordinates without knowing the source datum and units.
Transform moving origins and moving targets to a common epoch before comparing positions or route costs.
Preserve uncertainty through transformations; do not imply extra precision from more decimal places.
A missing or incompatible transform is an operational limitation, not permission to guess silently.
Transform chains must be testable against round-trip and known-reference cases within declared tolerances.
Galactocentric coordinates are a useful shared cartographic language, not an absolute motionless grid for the entire galaxy.

historicalNavigationEras.rule: These are candidate capability phases, not locked dates or a mandatory linear progression. Multiple frames coexist; remote polities can use different conventions, and a mature polity may retain local frames for practical reasons.

chartRecordContract.historicalRule: A superseded chart remains a valid historical artifact describing what its authors knew, assumed, or wanted users to believe. It must not silently replace present authoritative coordinates.

equipmentCapabilityModel.principle: Navigation capability emerges from sensors, clocks, computation, stored data, calibration, crew qualifications, power, maintenance, communications, and the environment—not from a technology label alone.
limitationsToModel: A chart may cover a destination but lack the precision required by the current drive or approach procedure.
A ship may possess a transform algorithm but lack the source data, clock agreement, or calibration needed to use it safely.
Long periods without updates increase uncertainty according to the relevant motion and clock model.
Damaged sensors, unqualified operators, power shortages, corrupted records, and incompatible standards degrade navigation.
High-end equipment does not guarantee success if route assumptions or source records are wrong.
Local arrival and docking require local observations and procedures even when a galaxy-scale chart exists.
